content:
In this part of Numbers chapter fifteen, Yahweh deals with what happened Numbers 15 draws a solemn line between sin committed unknowingly and sin committed defiantly. For the unintentional sin, Yahweh provided sacrifice, atonement, and forgiveness. But for the person who knowingly acted with a high hand, deliberately despising God's Word, the fearful sentence was that the person was to be cut off. For us, the New Creation, this distinction should give us both great comfort and holy fear. Today let us take up the first half of it, the comfort, and learn how God deals with the sin we did not even know we were committing.

The truth is that there are sins we commit without realizing them. Sometimes we speak carelessly, and only afterward do we understand that our words wounded someone. We may judge another person's motives without knowing the truth of their heart. We may follow a certain practice for years, and only later discover from Scripture that it was wrong all along. We may act selfishly without at first recognizing how deeply self-interest was controlling us.

There may even be weaknesses in our character that others around us can see long before we ever recognize them in ourselves. David understood this problem well, and he prayed, "Who can understand his errors? Cleanse me from secret faults" (Psalm 19:12). David knew that a man may carry faults he cannot even see, and so he asked God to cleanse him from the very sins he did not know were there.

The beautiful lesson of Numbers 15 is that ignorance did not leave Israel without provision. Yahweh provided atonement even for the sin that had been done unknowingly. And in the same way, the New Creation has a far greater sacrifice, not another bull or another goat, but Christ Himself. Those ancient sacrifices were only shadows, pointing forward to the one true Sin-Bearer, whose sacrifice truly deals with sin and provides real cleansing. John writes, "The blood of Jesus Christ His Son cleanses us from all sin" (1 John 1:7). Notice those words, "all sin." This includes the sins we clearly recognize, and also the failures that God must still bring into the light for us. This does not mean that ignorance makes sin unimportant, for Numbers 15 itself shows that unintentional sin still required atonement. Rather, it means that the sacrifice of Christ is fully sufficient, even for the failures we did not at first understand.

So, when God reveals such a sin to us, the New Creation should never try to defend it or explain it away. Instead, we confess it, we receive His cleansing, we correct whatever needs to be corrected, and we continue walking in the light. John gives us this beautiful assurance, "If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness" (1 John 1:9). When our conscience is stained, we do not repair it by pretending the stain is not there. We come to Yahweh, we confess, and we trust the cleansing that He has already provided for us in Christ. There is no need to hide, and no need to run from Him. The very God who exposes the fault is the God who stands ready to wash it away.

This is a wonderful comfort for every tender heart that walks with God.

Many sincere believers are troubled, wondering about the faults they cannot yet see, the failures still hidden even from themselves. But the provision of Numbers 15, fulfilled in Christ, answers that fear. God does not deal with us only according to the sins we happen to notice. He deals with us according to the perfect sacrifice of His Son, whose blood reaches even to the faults we have not yet discovered. As He shines His light into our hearts and shows us one thing after another, we simply keep confessing, keep receiving His cleansing, and keep walking forward. The discovery of a hidden sin is never a reason to despair. It is an invitation to come again into the light and be washed once more. Yet there is another side to this passage, a far more solemn one, for Numbers 15 does not stop with the sin of ignorance. It goes on to speak of a very different kind of sinner, and a very different ending. That is where we will continue tomorrow.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our faithful God, whose light searches the deepest places of the heart,
We thank You that You provided atonement even for the sin done in ignorance.

Cleanse us from the secret faults we cannot see, as David once prayed.

When You reveal a hidden sin, keep us from defending it, and teach us to confess it quickly.

We thank You that the blood of Christ cleanses us from all sin, even the sin we did not know.

Let the discovery of our faults drive us not into despair, but back into Your light.

"Who can understand his errors? Cleanse me from secret faults." - Psalm 19:12

In Christ name we pray. Amen.
